title.sr: Kako funkcionišu evropska tržišta električne energije

summary.en: A plain-language introduction to how electricity is traded and delivered across Europe.
summary.sr: Jednostavan uvod u to kako se električna energija trguje i isporučuje širom Evrope.

description.en: A plain-language introduction to how electricity is bought, sold and delivered across Europe: how forward, day-ahead, intraday and balancing markets fit together, and how national markets are linked across borders. This is the starting point for the rest of the Power Academy and for the price, spread and flow analytics in this dashboard.
description.sr: Jednostavan uvod u to kako se električna energija kupuje, prodaje i isporučuje širom Evrope: kako se terminsko, day-ahead, intraday i balansno tržište uklapaju i kako su nacionalna tržišta povezana preko granica. Ovo je polazna tačka za ostatak Power Academy i za analitiku cena, spredova i tokova u ovom dashboardu.

title.en: Day-Ahead: How SEEPEX Forms the Price

summary.en: How the next-day auction turns buy and sell orders into one clearing price.
summary.sr: Kako aukcija za sutrašnji dan pretvara ponude za kupovinu i prodaju u jednu cenu poravnanja.

description.en: Why does Serbia's price differ from Hungary's or Croatia's? This episode follows the day-ahead auction on SEEPEX: orders for tomorrow, the close of the order book at 11:00, and a simplified worked example with illustrative figures showing how the last accepted offer sets a single marginal clearing price. It then sets the Serbian auction beside EU market coupling, where one algorithm weighs supply, demand and cross-border limits.
description.sr: Zašto se cena u Srbiji razlikuje od cene u Mađarskoj ili Hrvatskoj? Ova epizoda prati day-ahead aukciju na SEEPEX-u: ponude za sutrašnji dan, zatvaranje knjige ponuda u 11:00 i pojednostavljen primer sa ilustrativnim vrednostima koji pokazuje kako poslednja prihvaćena ponuda određuje jednu marginalnu cenu poravnanja. Zatim poredi srpsku aukciju sa povezivanjem tržišta u EU, gde jedan algoritam istovremeno razmatra ponudu, potražnju i prekogranična ograničenja.

learn.en: Why neighbouring markets can price the same hour differently
learn.sr: Zašto susedna tržišta isti sat mogu da cene različito

learn.en: How the day-ahead auction works: orders for tomorrow, closing at 11:00
learn.sr: Kako radi day-ahead aukcija: ponude za sutra, zatvaranje u 11:00

learn.en: Marginal pricing: the last accepted offer sets the price, not the average
learn.sr: Marginalno formiranje cene: poslednja prihvaćena ponuda određuje cenu, a ne prosek

learn.en: How EU market coupling and its 15-minute products differ from SEEPEX's hourly products
learn.sr: Po čemu se povezivanje tržišta u EU i njegovi 15-minutni proizvodi razlikuju od SEEPEX-ovih časovnih proizvoda

title.sr: Intraday: trgovina kada se prognoze menjaju

summary.en: How traders correct a position after the auction, and why there is no single intraday price.
summary.sr: Kako trgovci ispravljaju poziciju posle aukcije i zašto ne postoji jedna intraday cena.

description.en: The day-ahead auction is over, but the weather keeps changing. This episode explains continuous intraday trading on SEEPEX through a worked example with illustrative figures: a solar producer that sold 40 MW for an hour, a forecast that drops to 30 MW, and a 10 MW buy-back. It shows an order book where bids and asks match at their own executed prices, how this differs from an auction, and why any deviation left at delivery still becomes an imbalance.
description.sr: Day-ahead aukcija je završena, ali vreme se i dalje menja. Ova epizoda objašnjava kontinuiranu intraday trgovinu na SEEPEX-u kroz primer sa ilustrativnim vrednostima: solarni proizvođač je prodao 40 MW za jedan sat, prognoza pada na 30 MW, a on otkupljuje 10 MW. Prikazuje knjigu ponuda u kojoj se ponude za kupovinu i prodaju sparuju po sopstvenim izvršenim cenama, po čemu se to razlikuje od aukcije i zašto svako odstupanje koje ostane do isporuke i dalje postaje debalans.

learn.en: Why intraday exists: forecasts change after the auction
learn.sr: Zašto postoji intraday: prognoze se menjaju posle aukcije

learn.en: A solar example: 40 MW sold, forecast falls to 30 MW, 10 MW bought back
learn.sr: Primer solarne elektrane: prodato 40 MW, prognoza pada na 30 MW, otkupljeno 10 MW

learn.en: Continuous order book: many executed prices, not one clearing price
learn.sr: Kontinuirana knjiga ponuda: mnogo izvršenih cena, a ne jedna cena poravnanja

learn.en: Hourly contracts that close 60 minutes before delivery; what remains becomes imbalance
learn.sr: Časovni ugovori koji se zatvaraju 60 minuta pre isporuke; ono što ostane postaje debalans

title.en: Balancing: What EMS Does in Real Time
title.sr: Balansiranje: šta EMS radi u realnom vremenu

summary.en: Who keeps the grid in balance after trading closes, and how imbalance is settled.
summary.sr: Ko održava mrežu u ravnoteži kada se trgovina zatvori i kako se debalans obračunava.

description.en: Electricity has to balance every second, even after trading has closed. This episode shows the role of Elektromreža Srbije (EMS) as transmission system operator, using an illustrative example of a producer scheduled for 30 MW that delivers 28 MW for 15 minutes, a deviation of 0.5 MWh. It separates a market party's financial imbalance settlement from EMS activating balancing resources, and distinguishes the day-ahead price, the price of activated balancing energy and the imbalance settlement price.
description.sr: Električna energija mora da bude u ravnoteži u svakoj sekundi, čak i kada se trgovina zatvori. Ova epizoda prikazuje ulogu Elektromreže Srbije (EMS) kao operatora prenosnog sistema, na ilustrativnom primeru proizvođača čiji je raspored 30 MW, a koji 15 minuta isporučuje 28 MW, odnosno odstupanje od 0,5 MWh. Razdvaja finansijski obračun debalansa tržišnog učesnika od aktiviranja balansnih resursa od strane EMS-a i razlikuje cenu na day-ahead tržištu, cenu aktivirane balansne energije i cenu obračuna debalansa.

learn.en: EMS as the Serbian transmission system operator
learn.sr: EMS kao operator prenosnog sistema Srbije

learn.en: Scheduled 30 MW, actual 28 MW for 15 minutes: 2 MW × 0.25 h = 0.5 MWh
learn.sr: Planirano 30 MW, ostvareno 28 MW tokom 15 minuta: 2 MW × 0,25 h = 0,5 MWh

learn.en: Financial imbalance settlement and physical system balancing are separate things
learn.sr: Finansijski obračun debalansa i fizičko balansiranje sistema nisu isto

learn.en: Three different prices: day-ahead, activated balancing energy, imbalance settlement
learn.sr: Tri različite cene: day-ahead, aktivirana balansna energija, obračun debalansa

title.en: Ancillary Services: FCR, aFRR and mFRR
title.sr: Pomoćne usluge: FCR, aFRR i mFRR

summary.en: The three layers of frequency reserves and the two ways they are paid.
summary.sr: Tri sloja rezervi frekvencije i dva načina na koja se plaćaju.

description.en: When a generator suddenly drops out, frequency starts to fall. This episode explains the three layers of reserves that respond: frequency containment reserve (FCR), automatic frequency restoration reserve (aFRR) and manually activated frequency restoration reserve (mFRR). It separates balancing capacity, the commitment to hold megawatts available, from activated balancing energy, the megawatt-hours actually delivered, and describes who can provide reserves, including storage and flexible demand where technically qualified.
description.sr: Kada generator iznenada ispadne, frekvencija počinje da pada. Ova epizoda objašnjava tri sloja rezervi koji reaguju: rezervu za zadržavanje frekvencije (FCR), automatsku rezervu za povratak frekvencije (aFRR) i ručno aktiviranu rezervu za povratak frekvencije (mFRR). Razdvaja balansni kapacitet, obavezu da megavati budu na raspolaganju, od aktivirane balansne energije, megavat-časova koji su stvarno isporučeni, i opisuje ko može da pruža rezerve, uključujući skladišta i fleksibilnu potrošnju kada su tehnički kvalifikovani.

learn.en: FCR contains, aFRR restores automatically, mFRR restores on instruction
learn.sr: FCR zadržava, aFRR automatski vraća frekvenciju, mFRR je vraća po nalogu

learn.en: EMS procures and activates reserves; who can qualify to provide them
learn.sr: EMS nabavlja i aktivira rezerve; ko može da se kvalifikuje da ih pruža

learn.en: Capacity (MW available) versus energy (MWh delivered): two separate payments
learn.sr: Kapacitet (raspoloživi MW) naspram energije (isporučeni MWh): dva odvojena plaćanja

learn.en: PICASSO and MARI as EU platforms, separate from Serbia's own arrangements
learn.sr: PICASSO i MARI kao evropske platforme, odvojene od sopstvenih aranžmana Srbije

title.en: Futures & Forwards: Hedging the Serbian Price
title.sr: Fjučersi i forvardi: zaštita od promene srpske cene

summary.en: How a financially settled future locks in a price, and what a hedge does not cover.
summary.sr: Kako finansijski poravnat fjučers fiksira cenu i šta hedž ne pokriva.

description.en: What if you must buy electricity next winter but do not know the spot price? This episode explains Serbian power futures, which are financially settled against the SEEPEX day-ahead reference price, with an illustrative hedge: a buyer locks in €100/MWh, spot rises to €130 and the future gains €30; spot falls to €70 and the future loses €30 while the physical purchase gets cheaper. It stresses that a hedge reduces price risk but leaves basis, volume, liquidity and credit risk, and that a financial future neither delivers electricity nor reserves cross-border capacity.
description.sr: Šta ako morate da kupite struju sledeće zime, a ne znate spot cenu? Ova epizoda objašnjava srpske fjučerse za električnu energiju, koji se finansijski poravnavaju prema referentnoj SEEPEX day-ahead ceni, na ilustrativnom primeru zaštite: kupac fiksira 100 €/MWh, spot raste na 130 €, a fjučers dobija 30 €; spot pada na 70 €, fjučers gubi 30 €, a fizička kupovina postaje jeftinija. Naglašava da hedž smanjuje cenovni rizik, ali ostavlja bazni, količinski, rizik likvidnosti i kreditni rizik, i da finansijski fjučers ne isporučuje struju niti rezerviše prekogranični kapacitet.

learn.en: The problem: next winter's price is uncertain
learn.sr: Problem: cena sledeće zime je neizvesna

learn.en: A long financial hedge at €100/MWh, with spot at €130 and at €70
learn.sr: Duga finansijska zaštita na 100 €/MWh, sa spotom na 130 € i na 70 €

learn.en: Financial future, physical delivery and cross-border capacity are three separate things
learn.sr: Finansijski fjučers, fizička isporuka i prekogranični kapacitet su tri odvojene stvari

learn.en: What a hedge leaves open: liquidity, volume, basis and credit risk
learn.sr: Šta hedž ostavlja otvorenim: rizik likvidnosti, količinski, bazni i kreditni rizik

title.en: Cross-Border Trading: Why Balkan Prices Diverge
title.sr: Prekogranična trgovina: zašto se cene na Balkanu razilaze

summary.en: Why a price spread is not profit, and how limited capacity keeps prices apart.
summary.sr: Zašto cenovni raspon nije profit i kako ograničen kapacitet drži cene razdvojenim.

description.en: Why can power cost more in Hungary than in Serbia at the same hour? This episode uses a hypothetical €60 against €120 spread to show that a spread alone is not profit: capacity rights, nominations, losses and trading costs all count. It shows how a congested line keeps prices apart, compares implicit allocation in coupled EU day-ahead markets with explicit allocation where markets are not coupled, and explains why the Balkans mix markets at different stages of integration.
description.sr: Zašto struja može da bude skuplja u Mađarskoj nego u Srbiji u isti sat? Ova epizoda koristi hipotetički raspon od 60 € naspram 120 € da pokaže da sam cenovni raspon nije profit: računaju se prava na kapacitet, nominacije, gubici i troškovi trgovine. Prikazuje kako zagušen vod drži cene razdvojenim, poredi implicitnu alokaciju na povezanim day-ahead tržištima EU sa eksplicitnom alokacijom tamo gde tržišta nisu povezana i objašnjava zašto Balkan spaja tržišta u različitim fazama integracije.

learn.en: Why the same hour can cost more in one country than another
learn.sr: Zašto isti sat može da košta više u jednoj zemlji nego u drugoj

learn.en: A spread is not profit: capacity, nomination, losses and costs
learn.sr: Raspon nije profit: kapacitet, nominacija, gubici i troškovi

learn.en: A congested line keeps prices apart
learn.sr: Zagušen vod drži cene razdvojenim

learn.en: Implicit allocation in coupled markets versus explicit allocation where markets are not coupled
learn.sr: Implicitna alokacija na povezanim tržištima naspram eksplicitne tamo gde tržišta nisu povezana

summary.en: How offers and bids become one clearing price, with a step-by-step merit-order example.

description.en: Why a day-ahead market exists, who trades in it and how orders are submitted. A simplified single-period uniform-price auction (illustrative figures) shows the merit order being built from three offers, demand added, and the last accepted offer setting the clearing price at 120 EUR/MWh, with every payment calculated. What-if cases show how lower demand or extra wind moves the price. The episode then covers European market coupling and congestion and SEEPEX as a regional example. It is a simplification and not a description of the EUPHEMIA algorithm.

learn.en: Why the day-ahead market exists and who takes part
Merit order: offers stacked from cheapest to most expensive
The last accepted offer sets one price for everyone
Why renewables and demand move the price
Market coupling and congestion

summary.en: How a position is corrected after the day-ahead auction: the order book, a worked trade and the SIDC auctions.

description.en: The day-ahead plan changes when forecasts do. This episode shows continuous intraday trading through an order book, where each trade is priced at the order already waiting, with a worked example (illustrative figures): a 30 MWh buy order matches 20 MWh at 78 EUR and 10 MWh at 82 EUR for an average of 79.33 EUR/MWh. It explains cross-border matching through SIDC and its dependence on available capacity, the three SIDC intraday auctions, and SEEPEX's continuous intraday market, launched in July 2023.

learn.en: Why intraday exists: forecasts change after the auction
The continuous order book: best bid, best offer, matching
A worked trade: different prices for each match
Cross-border matching and the SIDC intraday auctions

summary.en: How the system operator balances the grid and how deviations are charged.

description.en: Generation must match consumption every second, but forecasts are never perfect. This episode explains balance responsible parties and their schedules, how the transmission system operator activates upward and downward balancing energy, and how the cost is recovered through the imbalance price in 15-minute settlement periods. A worked example (illustrative figures) settles two portfolios, one short by 30 MWh and one long by 20 MWh, at 150 EUR/MWh. It closes with the role of EMS in Serbia.

learn.en: Balance responsible parties and their schedules
Short, long and the system imbalance
Upward and downward balancing energy
The imbalance price and 15-minute settlement periods

title.en: Ancillary Services: FCR, aFRR and mFRR

summary.en: The three layers of reserves that stop a frequency fall and restore 50 Hz.

description.en: What happens to frequency when a plant trips and how three reserves respond one after another: FCR (frequency containment reserve, full activation within 30 seconds), aFRR (automatic restoration, about five minutes) and mFRR (manual restoration, about 12.5 minutes). It introduces the European platforms PICASSO (aFRR) and MARI (mFRR) and separates the capacity payment for availability from the energy payment for activation with an illustrative battery example: 320 EUR for availability plus 180 EUR for activation.

learn.en: Frequency, and why it falls when a plant trips
FCR contains, aFRR and mFRR restore
PICASSO and MARI as European platforms
Capacity versus energy payments for reserve providers

summary.en: How a supplier locks in a margin with futures, and what it gives up.

description.en: A supplier sells at a fixed price but buys on a moving market. This episode contrasts forwards and exchange-traded futures with a clearing house, explains standard products (month, quarter, year, baseload) and works through a hedge with illustrative figures: 10 MW of baseload (87,600 MWh) sold at 85 EUR/MWh and hedged at 80 EUR/MWh locks in a 438,000 EUR margin whether spot ends at 110 or 60. It also covers daily variation margin and liquidity, and regional examples such as the EEX Phelix-DE baseload future and Hungarian power futures.

learn.en: Forwards versus futures and the role of the clearing house
Baseload products: month, quarter, year
A hedge locks the margin: results at spot 110 and spot 60
Variation margin and liquidity planning

summary.en: Why scarce interconnector capacity splits prices, and how coupling uses it.

description.en: Explains cross-border capacity and congestion, explicit versus implicit allocation, and how market coupling sends power from low-price to high-price zones. A two-zone example with illustrative supply curves shows prices of 50 and 90 EUR/MWh converging to about 63 EUR/MWh with enough capacity, and staying apart at 57.50 and 75 EUR/MWh when the line is limited to 15 MWh, yielding a congestion income of 262.50 EUR. It also introduces flow-based capacity calculation and the situation in Southeast Europe.

learn.en: Why interconnector capacity is scarce
Explicit versus implicit allocation
A two-zone coupling example: converging and congested prices
Flow-based capacity calculation
